speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
आहारस्त्वपि सर्वस्य त्रिविधो भवति प्रियः ।
यज्ञस्तपस्तथा दानं तेषां भेदमिमं शृणु ॥
iast:
āhārastvapi sarvasya trividho bhavati priyaḥ |
yajñastapastathā dānaṃ teṣāṃ bhedamimaṃ śṛṇu ||
english: Even the food that each person likes is of three kinds, and so are sacrifice, austerity and giving. Hear how they differ.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
आयुःसत्त्वबलारोग्यसुखप्रीतिविवर्धनाः ।
रस्याः स्निग्धाः स्थिरा हृद्या आहाराः सात्त्विकप्रियाः ॥
iast:
āyuḥsattvabalārogyasukhaprītivivardhanāḥ |
rasyāḥ snigdhāḥ sthirā hṛdyā āhārāḥ sāttvikapriyāḥ ||
english: Foods that increase life, vitality, strength, health, happiness and good cheer, that are tasty, rich, substantial and pleasing to the heart, are dear to the sattvic.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
कट्‌वम्ललवणात्युष्णतीक्ष्णरूक्षविदाहिनः ।
आहारा राजसस्येष्टा दुःखशोकामयप्रदाः ॥
iast:
kaṭvamlalavaṇātyuṣṇatīkṣṇarūkṣavidāhinaḥ |
āhārā rājasasyeṣṭā duḥkhaśokāmayapradāḥ ||
english: Foods that are bitter, sour, salty, very hot, pungent, dry and burning are liked by the rajasic; they bring pain, grief and illness.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यातयामं गतरसं पूति पर्युषितं च यत् ।
उच्छिष्टमपि चामेध्यं भोजनं तामसप्रियम् ॥
iast:
yātayāmaṃ gatarasaṃ pūti paryuṣitaṃ ca yat |
ucchiṣṭamapi cāmedhyaṃ bhojanaṃ tāmasapriyam ||
english: Food that is stale, tasteless, putrid and left overnight, food that is leftover and impure, is dear to the tamasic.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्यज्ञो विधिदृष्टो य इज्यते ।
यष्टव्यमेवेति मनः समाधाय स सात्त्विकः ॥
iast:
aphalākāṅkṣibhiryajño vidhidṛṣṭo ya ijyate |
yaṣṭavyameveti manaḥ samādhāya sa sāttvikaḥ ||
english: Sacrifice that is offered according to the rules by those who seek no reward, with the mind settled on the thought that it simply ought to be done, is sattvic.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अभिसंधाय तु फलं दम्भार्थमपि चैव यत् ।
इज्यते भरतश्रेष्ठ तं यज्ञं विद्धि राजसम् ॥
iast:
abhisaṃdhāya tu phalaṃ dambhārthamapi caiva yat |
ijyate bharataśreṣṭha taṃ yajñaṃ viddhi rājasam ||
english: But sacrifice offered with an eye on the reward, or for the sake of show, best of the Bharatas, know that sacrifice to be rajasic.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
विधिहीनमसृष्टान्नं मन्त्रहीनमदक्षिणम् ।
श्रद्धाविरहितं यज्ञं तामसं परिचक्षते ॥
iast:
vidhihīnamasṛṣṭānnaṃ mantrahīnamadakṣiṇam |
śraddhāvirahitaṃ yajñaṃ tāmasaṃ paricakṣate ||
english: Sacrifice that ignores the rules, in which no food is shared, no sacred words are said and no gifts are given, and which lacks faith, is called tamasic.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
देवद्विजगुरुप्राज्ञपूजनं शौचमार्जवम् ।
ब्रह्मचर्यमहिंसा च शारीरं तप उच्यते ॥
iast:
devadvijaguruprājñapūjanaṃ śaucamārjavam |
brahmacaryamahiṃsā ca śārīraṃ tapa ucyate ||
english: Reverence for the gods, the twice-born, teachers and the wise; purity, honesty, celibacy and non-violence: this is called austerity of the body.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत् ।
स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते ॥
iast:
anudvegakaraṃ vākyaṃ satyaṃ priyahitaṃ ca yat |
svādhyāyābhyasanaṃ caiva vāṅmayaṃ tapa ucyate ||
english: Speech that causes no distress, that is true, pleasant and beneficial, and the regular study of scripture: this is called austerity of speech.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
मनः प्रसादः सौम्यत्वं मौनमात्मविनिग्रहः ।
भावसंशुद्धिरित्येतत्तपो मानसमुच्यते ॥
iast:
manaḥ prasādaḥ saumyatvaṃ maunamātmavinigrahaḥ |
bhāvasaṃśuddhirityetattapo mānasamucyate ||
english: Serenity of mind, gentleness, silence, self-control and purity of heart: this is called austerity of the mind.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
श्रद्धया परया तप्तं तपस्तत्त्रिविधं नरैः ।
अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्युक्तैः सात्त्विकं परिचक्षते ॥
iast:
śraddhayā parayā taptaṃ tapastattrividhaṃ naraiḥ |
aphalākāṅkṣibhiryuktaiḥ sāttvikaṃ paricakṣate ||
english: This threefold austerity, practised with supreme faith by disciplined people who seek no reward, is called sattvic.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
सत्कारमानपूजार्थं तपो दम्भेन चैव यत् ।
क्रियते तदिह प्रोक्तं राजसं चलमध्रुवम् ॥
iast:
satkāramānapūjārthaṃ tapo dambhena caiva yat |
kriyate tadiha proktaṃ rājasaṃ calamadhruvam ||
english: Austerity practised to gain respect, honour and reverence, and out of hypocrisy, is called rajasic here: unstable and fleeting.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
मूढग्राहेणात्मनो यत्पीडया क्रियते तपः ।
परस्योत्सादनार्थं वा तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥
iast:
mūḍhagrāheṇātmano yatpīḍayā kriyate tapaḥ |
parasyotsādanārthaṃ vā tattāmasamudāhṛtam ||
english: Austerity practised out of foolish obstinacy, with self-torture, or to bring ruin on another, is called tamasic.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
दातव्यमिति यद्दानं दीयतेऽनुपकारिणे ।
देशे काले च पात्रे च तद्दानं सात्त्विकं स्मृतम् ॥
iast:
dātavyamiti yaddānaṃ dīyate'nupakāriṇe |
deśe kāle ca pātre ca taddānaṃ sāttvikaṃ smṛtam ||
english: A gift given because it is right to give, to one who can give nothing in return, at the proper place and time and to a worthy person, is held to be sattvic.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यत्तु प्रत्युपकारार्थं फलमुद्दिश्य वा पुनः ।
दीयते च परिक्लिष्टं तद्दानं राजसं स्मृतम् ॥
iast:
yattu pratyupakārārthaṃ phalamuddiśya vā punaḥ |
dīyate ca parikliṣṭaṃ taddānaṃ rājasaṃ smṛtam ||
english: But a gift given in hope of something in return, or with an eye on the reward, or given grudgingly, is held to be rajasic.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अदेशकाले यद्दानमपात्रेभ्यश्च दीयते ।
असत्कृतमवज्ञातं तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥
iast:
adeśakāle yaddānamapātrebhyaśca dīyate |
asatkṛtamavajñātaṃ tattāmasamudāhṛtam ||
english: A gift given at the wrong place or time to unworthy people, without respect or with contempt, is called tamasic.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
ॐतत्सदिति निर्देशो ब्रह्मणस्त्रिविधः स्मृतः ।
ब्राह्मणास्तेन वेदाश्च यज्ञाश्च विहिताः पुरा ॥
iast:
oṃtatsaditi nirdeśo brahmaṇastrividhaḥ smṛtaḥ |
brāhmaṇāstena vedāśca yajñāśca vihitāḥ purā ||
english: 'Om tat sat' is held to be the threefold designation of Brahman. By it, of old, the brahmins, the Vedas and the sacrifices were ordained.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
तस्मादोमित्युदाहृत्य यज्ञदानतपःक्रियाः ।
प्रवर्तन्ते विधानोक्ताः सततं ब्रह्मवादिनाम् ॥
iast:
tasmādomityudāhṛtya yajñadānatapaḥkriyāḥ |
pravartante vidhānoktāḥ satataṃ brahmavādinām ||
english: So those who follow the Veda always begin their acts of sacrifice, giving and austerity, as prescribed, by uttering 'Om'.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
तदित्यनभिसन्धाय फलं यज्ञतपःक्रियाः ।
दानक्रियाश्च विविधाः क्रियन्ते मोक्षकाङ्क्षिभिः ॥
iast:
tadityanabhisandhāya phalaṃ yajñatapaḥkriyāḥ |
dānakriyāśca vividhāḥ kriyante mokṣakāṅkṣibhiḥ ||
english: Uttering 'tat', seekers of liberation perform the various acts of sacrifice, austerity and giving without aiming at any reward.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
सद्भावे साधुभावे च सदित्येतत्प्रयुज्यते ।
प्रशस्ते कर्मणि तथा सच्छब्दः पार्थ युज्यते ॥
iast:
sadbhāve sādhubhāve ca sadityetatprayujyate |
praśaste karmaṇi tathā sacchabdaḥ pārtha yujyate ||
english: The word 'sat' is used to mean reality and goodness; and, son of Pritha, the word 'sat' is also used for a praiseworthy act.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यज्ञे तपसि दाने च स्थितिः सदिति चोच्यते ।
कर्म चैव तदर्थीयं सदित्येवाभिधीयते ॥
iast:
yajñe tapasi dāne ca sthitiḥ saditi cocyate |
karma caiva tadarthīyaṃ sadityevābhidhīyate ||
english: Steadfastness in sacrifice, austerity and giving is also called 'sat', and any action done for that purpose is likewise called 'sat'.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अश्रद्धया हुतं दत्तं तपस्तप्तं कृतं च यत् ।
असदित्युच्यते पार्थ न च तत्प्रेत्य नो इह ॥
iast:
aśraddhayā hutaṃ dattaṃ tapastaptaṃ kṛtaṃ ca yat |
asadityucyate pārtha na ca tatpretya no iha ||
english: Whatever is offered, given or done, and whatever austerity is practised without faith, is called 'asat', son of Pritha; it is of no use here or hereafter.

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
संन्यासस्य महाबाहो तत्त्वमिच्छामि वेदितुम् ।
त्यागस्य च हृषीकेश पृथक्केशिनिषूदन ॥
iast:
saṃnyāsasya mahābāho tattvamicchāmi veditum |
tyāgasya ca hṛṣīkeśa pṛthakkeśiniṣūdana ||
english: Mighty-armed one, I wish to know the truth about renunciation, Krishna, and about relinquishment, and how they differ.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
काम्यानां कर्मणां न्यासं संन्यासं कवयो विदुः ।
सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं प्राहुस्त्यागं विचक्षणाः ॥
iast:
kāmyānāṃ karmaṇāṃ nyāsaṃ saṃnyāsaṃ kavayo viduḥ |
sarvakarmaphalatyāgaṃ prāhustyāgaṃ vicakṣaṇāḥ ||
english: The wise understand renunciation as giving up actions driven by desire; the discerning call giving up the fruits of all actions relinquishment.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
त्याज्यं दोषवदित्येके कर्म प्राहुर्मनीषिणः ।
यज्ञदानतपःकर्म न त्याज्यमिति चापरे ॥
iast:
tyājyaṃ doṣavadityeke karma prāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ |
yajñadānatapaḥkarma na tyājyamiti cāpare ||
english: Some thinkers say that action should be given up as if it were a fault; others say that acts of sacrifice, giving and austerity should not be given up.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
निश्चयं शृणु मे तत्र त्यागे भरतसत्तम ।
त्यागो हि पुरुषव्याघ्र त्रिविधः संप्रकीर्तितः ॥
iast:
niścayaṃ śṛṇu me tatra tyāge bharatasattama |
tyāgo hi puruṣavyāghra trividhaḥ saṃprakīrtitaḥ ||
english: Now hear my conclusion about relinquishment, best of the Bharatas; for relinquishment, tiger among men, is declared to be of three kinds.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यज्ञदानतपःकर्म न त्याज्यं कार्यमेव तत् ।
यज्ञो दानं तपश्चैव पावनानि मनीषिणाम् ॥
iast:
yajñadānatapaḥkarma na tyājyaṃ kāryameva tat |
yajño dānaṃ tapaścaiva pāvanāni manīṣiṇām ||
english: Acts of sacrifice, giving and austerity should not be given up; they should be done. Sacrifice, giving and austerity purify the wise.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
एतान्यपि तु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलानि च ।
कर्तव्यानीति मे पार्थ निश्चितं मतमुत्तमम् ॥
iast:
etānyapi tu karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā phalāni ca |
kartavyānīti me pārtha niścitaṃ matamuttamam ||
english: But even these actions should be done giving up attachment and their fruits: this, son of Pritha, is my settled and highest view.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
नियतस्य तु संन्यासः कर्मणो नोपपद्यते ।
मोहात्तस्य परित्यागस्तामसः परिकीर्तितः ॥
iast:
niyatasya tu saṃnyāsaḥ karmaṇo nopapadyate |
mohāttasya parityāgastāmasaḥ parikīrtitaḥ ||
english: Renouncing a prescribed duty is not right; giving it up out of delusion is declared to be tamasic.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
दुःखमित्येव यत्कर्म कायक्लेशभयात्त्यजेत् ।
स कृत्वा राजसं त्यागं नैव त्यागफलं लभेत् ॥
iast:
duḥkhamityeva yatkarma kāyakleśabhayāttyajet |
sa kṛtvā rājasaṃ tyāgaṃ naiva tyāgaphalaṃ labhet ||
english: One who gives up action because it is painful, out of fear of bodily hardship, makes a rajasic relinquishment and does not gain its fruit.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
कार्यमित्येव यत्कर्म नियतं क्रियतेऽर्जुन ।
सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलं चैव स त्यागः सात्त्विको मतः ॥
iast:
kāryamityeva yatkarma niyataṃ kriyate'rjuna |
saṅgaṃ tyaktvā phalaṃ caiva sa tyāgaḥ sāttviko mataḥ ||
english: When a prescribed action is done simply because it ought to be done, Arjuna, giving up attachment and its fruit, that relinquishment is held to be sattvic.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
न द्वेष्ट्यकुशलं कर्म कुशले नानुषज्जते ।
त्यागी सत्त्वसमाविष्टो मेधावी छिन्नसंशयः ॥
iast:
na dveṣṭyakuśalaṃ karma kuśale nānuṣajjate |
tyāgī sattvasamāviṣṭo medhāvī chinnasaṃśayaḥ ||
english: The relinquisher, filled with sattva, wise and free of doubt, neither dislikes unpleasant work nor clings to pleasant work.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
न हि देहभृता शक्यं त्यक्तुं कर्माण्यशेषतः ।
यस्तु कर्मफलत्यागी स त्यागीत्यभिधीयते ॥
iast:
na hi dehabhṛtā śakyaṃ tyaktuṃ karmāṇyaśeṣataḥ |
yastu karmaphalatyāgī sa tyāgītyabhidhīyate ||
english: It is not possible for an embodied being to give up actions entirely; but one who gives up the fruit of action is called a relinquisher.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अनिष्टमिष्टं मिश्रं च त्रिविधं कर्मणः फलम् ।
भवत्यत्यागिनां प्रेत्य न तु संन्यासिनां क्वचित् ॥
iast:
aniṣṭamiṣṭaṃ miśraṃ ca trividhaṃ karmaṇaḥ phalam |
bhavatyatyāgināṃ pretya na tu saṃnyāsināṃ kvacit ||
english: Unwanted, wanted and mixed: the fruit of action is of three kinds, and it comes after death to those who have not relinquished, but never to those who have renounced.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
पञ्चैतानि महाबाहो कारणानि निबोध मे ।
सांख्ये कृतान्ते प्रोक्तानि सिद्धये सर्वकर्मणाम् ॥
iast:
pañcaitāni mahābāho kāraṇāni nibodha me |
sāṃkhye kṛtānte proktāni siddhaye sarvakarmaṇām ||
english: Learn from me, mighty-armed one, the five causes for the accomplishment of all actions, as taught in the Sankhya doctrine.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अधिष्ठानं तथा कर्ता करणं च पृथग्विधम् ।
विविधाश्च पृथक्चेष्टा दैवं चैवात्र पञ्चमम् ॥
iast:
adhiṣṭhānaṃ tathā kartā karaṇaṃ ca pṛthagvidham |
vividhāśca pṛthakceṣṭā daivaṃ caivātra pañcamam ||
english: The seat of action, the doer, the various instruments, the many kinds of effort, and fifth, the divine.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
शरीरवाङ्‌मनोभिर्यत्कर्म प्रारभते नरः ।
न्याय्यं वा विपरीतं वा पञ्चैते तस्य हेतवः ॥
iast:
śarīravāṅmanobhiryatkarma prārabhate naraḥ |
nyāyyaṃ vā viparītaṃ vā pañcaite tasya hetavaḥ ||
english: Whatever action a person undertakes with body, speech or mind, whether right or wrong, these five are its causes.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
तत्रैवं सति कर्तारमात्मानं केवलं तु यः ।
पश्यत्यकृतबुद्धित्वान्न स पश्यति दुर्मतिः ॥
iast:
tatraivaṃ sati kartāramātmānaṃ kevalaṃ tu yaḥ |
paśyatyakṛtabuddhitvānna sa paśyati durmatiḥ ||
english: That being so, one who, through lack of understanding, sees the self alone as the doer, does not see, being of poor understanding.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यस्य नाहंकृतो भावो बुद्धिर्यस्य न लिप्यते ।
हत्वापि स इमाँल्लोकान्न हन्ति न निबध्यते ॥
iast:
yasya nāhaṃkṛto bhāvo buddhiryasya na lipyate |
hatvāpi sa imām̐llokānna hanti na nibadhyate ||
english: One who is free of the sense of 'I am the doer', whose understanding is not tainted, even if they kill these people, does not kill and is not bound.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं परिज्ञाता त्रिविधा कर्मचोदना ।
करणं कर्म कर्तेति त्रिविधः कर्मसंग्रहः ॥
iast:
jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ parijñātā trividhā karmacodanā |
karaṇaṃ karma karteti trividhaḥ karmasaṃgrahaḥ ||
english: Knowledge, the object of knowledge and the knower are the threefold impulse to action; the instrument, the action and the doer are the threefold basis of action.
